Fission Yeast Stress Time Course (three contrasts)

Source: R/datasets.R
stress_timecourse.Rd

Real DESeq2 results from an RNA-seq time course of wild-type fission yeast (Schizosaccharomyces pombe) exposed to osmotic stress (1 M sorbitol). Each element of the list compares one time point after stress with time 0, so the list can be passed straight to ggvolc to compare the contrasts side by side. The response is strongest at 30 minutes and fades by 180 minutes.

Usage

stress_timecourse

Format

A named list of three data frames, "30 min", "60 min", and "180 min", each with 6535 rows and the columns:

genes

Character. Gene symbol, or the systematic ID when no symbol exists.

baseMean

Numeric. Mean of normalized counts across all samples.

log2FoldChange

Numeric. log2 fold change versus time 0.

pvalue

Numeric. Wald test p-value.

padj

Numeric. Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value.

Source

Leong HS, Dawson K, Wirth C, et al. (2014). A global non-coding RNA system modulates fission yeast protein levels in response to stress. Nature Communications 5:3947. doi:10.1038/ncomms4947 . GEO accession GSE56761. Data via the Bioconductor package fission.

Details

The counts come from the Bioconductor data package fission (wild-type samples only, 3 replicates per time point; genes with fewer than 10 reads in total removed). Results were computed with DESeq2::DESeq() using design = ~ minute; see data-raw/stress_timecourse.R in the package sources. As in any DESeq2 output, padj is NA for genes removed by independent filtering.

Examples

names(stress_timecourse)
#> [1] "30 min"  "60 min"  "180 min"
ggvolc(stress_timecourse, label_top = 5, show_counts = TRUE)
#> ggvolc: left out 384 gene(s) with NA padj or log2FoldChange (e.g. genes DESeq2 filtered as low-count or outliers).
